originalContent.title: National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR) (2018–2025):
originalContent.summary: Schemes — National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR) (2018–2025):

items: The NAPDDR aims to reduce drug and alcohol dependency through prevention, treatment, and
rehabilitation. It includes two main components:
 Help to Alcohol Victims: 90% financial support for treatment and rehabilitation.
 Social Security Assistance: 90% financial aid for social security initiatives.
The plan focuses on awareness campaigns, community interventions, professional training, treatment
centers, and legal frameworks to effectively tackle substance abuse.

blocks.title: National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR) & Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan
blocks.summary: To employ a multi-pronged strategy involving preventive education, awareness generation, identification, counseling, treatment, and whole-person recovery and rehabilitation of substance-dependent individuals.

rows: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
₹260+ Crore annual allocation under MoSJE Social Defence budget.
100% Central Sector Scheme (100% Central assistance to State Governments/UTs and NGOs).
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, National Institute of Social Defence (NISD), State Social Welfare Departments, and accredited NGOs.

items: **Target Beneficiaries:** Individuals, youth, vulnerable communities, and families affected by substance abuse across India.
**Eligibility Criteria:** Any substance-dependent individual seeking treatment or community intervention; NGOs/institutions running rehabilitation centres.
Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA): Flagship mass awareness campaign launched on 15 August 2020 in 272 vulnerable districts, now expanded nationwide to 372+ districts.
Integrated Rehabilitation Centres for Addicts (IRCAs): Over 340+ IRCAs funded to provide free counseling, de-addiction medical treatment, and whole-person recovery.
Community based Peer Led Intervention (CPLI): Engages youth and peer educators for early vulnerability identification in children/adolescents.
Outreach and Drop In Centres (ODICs): Safe screening and harm reduction spaces.
National Toll-Free Helpline: "14446" (Tele-counseling helpline for de-addiction).
Flagship Campaign: Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA) launched 15 Aug 2020.
Funding pattern: 100% Central Sector (Government provides up to 100% financial assistance for IRCAs/ODICs).
